about.description: I’m a web developer who loves building websites that look amazing and work smoothly. Since diving into this world, I’ve developed a sharp eye for design, a knack for clean code, and a real obsession with making sure users have the best experience possible. Whether it’s front-end development, UI/UX design, or digital branding, I get excited about turning ideas into polished, fully functional sites. For me, it’s all about mixing creativity with technical skill, so that the end result isn’t just beautiful, but also fast, responsive, and easy to use.

list.name: Dar'Loca
list.tagline: A car rental management, built for how Moroccan agencies actually work.
list.text: A full-featured platform for car rental businesses, including bookings, invoices, dashboards and more.
list.studyText: Most car rental agencies in Morocco run on a mix of WhatsApp, paper contracts and a shared Excel sheet, no shared view of which car is out, which contract is expiring, or which client just walked in twice under two different names. Dar'Loca is a self-hosted SaaS platform I designed and built end to end, frontend, backend, infrastructure and deployment, to replace that with one system an agency actually runs its day from.
list.challenge: Agencies needed something that fit their existing paperwork-heavy, French-language workflow, not a generic fleet-management tool built for a different market. Contracts had to look and print the way a client already expected. Client identity had to be captured reliably from ID cards and passports, by staff who won't type long forms during a handover. And the whole thing had to run reliably on a single low-cost server, not a cloud stack an agency owner would never be able to afford or manage.
list.solution: I built the fleet planner around drag-to-create bookings so an agency can go from calendar to signed contract in a few clicks, added camera-based ID scanning that reads Moroccan CIN cards, passports and EU ID cards and fills the client form automatically, and wired electronic signature capture with an IP and geolocation audit trail so contracts hold up as evidence. The whole platform runs on a single VPS I manage myself, Nginx, PM2, PostgreSQL, which keeps hosting costs low enough that the economics work for a small agency.

list.name: Infinite Padel Courts
list.tagline: A dated construction site rebuilt into an interactive, made-to-measure experience.
list.text: Custom 3D configurator and full redesign for a padel court construction company.
list.studyText: Infinite Padel Courts came to me with a site that looked like most others in the construction space: stock photography, generic layouts, and 3D renders pulled from unrelated sources that didn't actually represent their work. I rebuilt the site from the ground up and replaced the visual identity entirely, modeling realistic court mockups in Blender under their own name, then built an interactive 3D court configurator on top of that so visitors could actually picture what they'd be buying.
list.challenge: Construction and sports-facility clients want to see the finished product before they commit, but padel courts have dozens of configurable variables: surface, wall height, lighting, fencing, cover type. A static gallery couldn't show that, and the existing renders weren't even Infinite Padel's own work. The configurator also had to work for non-technical visitors on both desktop and mobile, with no sign-up friction, since most visitors are evaluating, not yet ready to register.
list.solution: I modeled a library of realistic, on-brand court mockups in Blender to replace the generic renders, then built a lightweight 3D configurator on top using Three.js, letting visitors swap surfaces, colors and structural options in real time with no account required. I rebuilt the rest of the site's layout and interaction design around that centerpiece, and made sure every part of it, configurator included, held up on mobile, not just desktop.

list.name: SimoLimo
list.tagline: A luxury booking experience for a Denver limousine company, built for an owner-operator.
list.text: Luxury limousine and premium car booking website for a Denver-based transportation company.
list.studyText: SimoLimo is built for an individual running his own luxury transportation business, someone who needed a site that could stand in for a full sales team: it had to look as premium as the cars themselves, make booking effortless for clients, and give him a direct, simple way to be contacted, without any of the overhead of managing a larger platform.
list.challenge: In the luxury transportation space, the website is often the first and only impression a client gets before booking a car worth six figures. It needed to feel high-end without feeling cold or corporate, since the business is run by one person, not a fleet company. On top of that, booking and contact had to be frictionless for clients who are often booking last-minute, from a phone, for an airport run or an event.
list.solution: I designed the site around a restrained, premium visual language, dark tones, strong photography, generous spacing, that reads as luxury without needing heavy ornamentation. I built an easy online booking flow alongside direct contact options, so a client can either book in a couple of steps or reach out to the owner directly, whichever fits the situation.

list.name: Infinite Sport
list.tagline: A motivating storefront and site for a company building MMA, gyms and stadium courts.
list.text: A modern, responsive website with an integrated online store for a company that builds gyms and wellness spaces.
list.studyText: Infinite Sport builds physical sports infrastructure, MMA and boxing rings, padel courts, football pitches, outdoor and stadium installations, and needed a site with the same energy as what they build. Beyond the marketing site, they needed a working WooCommerce store where some products aren't one-size-fits-all: certain items needed to be customizable by the customer before purchase, plus CRM integration to actually capture and follow up on leads.
list.challenge: A construction/equipment company selling across several very different sport categories risks feeling generic if the site treats every product the same way. The site needed to feel motivating and energetic rather than corporate, while still functioning as a real e-commerce store. Some products couldn't just be sold as-is: customers needed to configure them before checkout, which standard WooCommerce doesn't handle out of the box. And leads coming through the site needed to flow into their CRM automatically, not get lost in an inbox.
list.solution: I built the site with interactive, energetic elements to match the brand across all their sport categories, then integrated WooCommerce for the store itself. For the products that needed configuration, I wrote custom code on top of WooCommerce so customers could customize those items to their specs before adding them to cart. I also wired up CRM integration, including cookie-based tracking, so leads and orders coming through the site feed directly into their sales pipeline instead of needing manual follow-up.
